html:
SMTO-EXE-0147 — The button or field SMTO needs is greyed out

GUID: 821ae63a-062d-5518-b438-cc08a7ece35e
Slug: ui-element-disabled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO found the button or field, but the app has it switched off (greyed out) right now, so it can't be used yet. SMTO didn't click or type anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses there), look at what the app is waiting for, such as a required field or a page still loading. Apps grey out a control until something else is done first.
  2. Complete that missing step yourself, or tell SMTO in a message what needs to be done first. Once the app's condition is met, the control switches back on.
  3. Ask SMTO to look at the app again and then do the action. SMTO checks again that the control is available before using it.

What success looks like

  • The control is no longer greyed out in the app, and SMTO's next step completes the action.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the app name and the control you wanted, to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't look for ways to force a greyed-out control; the app may be blocking it for a reason.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • UI mutation preflight found the selected native element's enabled flag false, so no action was dispatched.

What this means

  • Mutation preflight found the selected native element's enabled flag false. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Mutation preflight found the selected native element's enabled flag false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the control's current enabled state and any application prerequisite that explains it, without guessing that prerequisite from the label alone.

How to fix it

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway to see the application's current state, satisfy the prerequisite that enables the control (required fields, selection, completed loading or dialog), then confirm the element reports enabled before the authorized action.
  • Inspect the application state and satisfy its actual prerequisite, then verify the control is enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway. Correct the target or prerequisites before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended control is observed enabled before the authorized action.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
